citations.narrative:
Four enclosures were not large enough to allow the birds contained within to make normal postural and social
adjustments and allow adequate freedom of movement. One enclosure measuring approximately 2ft X 3ft contained 21
green cheeked parakeets and another similar sized enclosure contained 21 cockatiels. A larger enclosure measuring
approximately 6ft X 4ft contained 57 cockatiels and another similar sized enclosure contained 150 parakeets. The number
and size of perches provided for the birds in these enclosures did not allow all birds to perch at the same time and have
normal social adjustments. In order to move to another perch, the birds had to displace other birds. Numerous birds were
forced to perch on the wire mesh walls or stand on the floor. The facility representative indicated the birds were recently
acquired and appeared in good health at the time of inspection.
Lack of ability to make normal postural and social adjustments may cause malnutrition, poor condition, stress, or
abnormal behaviors. Each bird must be able to make normal postural and social adjustments with adequate freedom of
movement and freedom to escape from aggression demonstrated by other animals.
Correct by 9/15/2026

The food receptacles for 6 Lorikeets housed in three separate enclosures contained nectar and had numerous ants
crawling on the inside and outside of the receptacles and contacting the nectar. The facility representative stated the
lorikeets were able to eat the nectar earlier in the day, pest free, but as the day progressed, the ants were attracted to the
feed. At the time of inspection, the lorikeets appeared in good body condition.
Contaminated feed can cause illness or health problems for the animals and may prevent them from obtaining necessary
nutrition. A system should be in place to ensure the food receptacles and nectar within provided to the lorikeets is
replaced as often as needed to minimize contamination due to pests. Food and any food receptacles must be located so
as to minimize any risk of contamination by excreta, precipitation, and pests. Food receptacles and feeding areas must be
kept clean.
Correct by 9/15/2026

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
Areas around the bird enclosures and in the large aviary were cluttered with items and waste that do not promote
standard housekeeping practices. In the large aviary, there was an accumulation of caging material on top of multiple
enclosures. In addition, discarded cages were stacked directly next to multiple enclosures housing birds outside of the
aviary. Free roaming pigs have deposited waste directly under enclosures housing birds and fly bags intended to control
pest populations were dry and expired.
Accumulations of unused items and animal waste can create breeding and living areas for rodents, pests, and vermin.
Premises where housing facilities are located, including buildings and surrounding grounds, must be kept clean and in
good repair in order to protect the birds from injury and disease, to facilitate the husbandry practices required in this
subpart. Premises must be kept free of accumulations of trash, junk, waste products, and discarded matter, for the health
and well-being of the birds.
Correct by 9/30/2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative.
Additional Inspectors:
ALEXANDRA ANDRICOS, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
